LM Information Technology Specialist Kyle Brown accepted the award on LM’s behalf. The EPEAT award recognizes organizations for excellence in sustainable procurement of electronic equipment. EPEAT is a method for purchasers to evaluate a product’s effect on the environment, rate it accordingly, and identify it as a preferable electronic good. Manufacturers register products in the EPEAT category based on the device’s ability to meet certain criteria, including product lifestyle, design, energy production, and recycling. pages.text: Lobito Corridor: Can Trump-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo and Angola? Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo? 3 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Akisa Wandera BBC Africa, Lobito AFP via Getty Images The Lobito Corridor links DR Congo's mineral-rich south to Angola's Atlantic coast through the Benguela Railway and the Port of Lobito As trains carrying thousands of tonnes of copper from the Democratic Republic of Congo roar through her community, 20-year-old Manuela Julia is not thinking about critical minerals or billion-dollar investments. She is thinking about getting around more easily. The railway runs through Catumbela, near the Angolan city of Lobito, on the Atlantic coast. For Julia, it has made travelling cheaper and more convenient. "Before, I had to use a taxi, which is much more expensive. Now it is cheaper and easier to travel," she says. But the railway has ambitions far bigger than improving local transport. It is part of the Lobito Corridor, a US-backed effort to secure access to Africa's critical minerals and promote regional economic cooperation, which Washington hopes will help bring peace to conflict-torn eastern DR Congo. Under agreements brokered by US President Donald Trump, DR Congo and neighbouring Rwanda have committed to greater economic cooperation, including more transparent mineral supply chains and regional infrastructure development. They Can Unlock the Rest of the Night Sky. Made up of three of summer’s brightest stars, the Summer Triangle is an easy starting point for exploring—and photographing—the Milky Way and beyond. The Milky Way arcs above the walls of a gorge, framed by the three bright stars of the Summer Triangle. BABAK TAFRESHI, National Geographic Image Collection By Stefanie Waldek Published August 20, 2026 Stargazing can feel overwhelming when you don’t know where to begin. But in August, three exceptionally bright stars offer an easy starting point. Vega, Deneb, and Altair form the Summer Triangle, an enormous star pattern that rises high in the evening sky across much of the Northern Hemisphere. Once you find it, the triangle can serve as a guide to nearby constellations, deep-sky objects, and the Milky Way. It is also one of the most photogenic regions of the summer sky in August. Here’s how to find the Summer Triangle—and photograph what surrounds it. How to Find the Summer Triangle The Summer Triangle is not a constellation, but an asterism, or a recognizable pattern of stars. Begin with Vega, one of the brightest stars visible from Earth. In mid-August, observers in the Northern Hemisphere can generally find it high overhead. Deneb appears to one side of Vega, while Altair lies farther away, creating a large, elongated triangle. pages.text: Look for This Colorful, Twinkling Star in the Night Sky This Fall | National Geographic SCIENCE NIGHT SKY GUIDE Look for This Colorful, Twinkling Star in the Night Sky This Fall On autumn evenings, Capella can put on a dazzling display of red, green, and blue. Here's why it happens and where to look. Venus, the Pleiades star cluster, and the bright star Capella rise in the dawn sky above a tufa formation in California’s Mono Lake. BABAK TAFRESHI, National Geographic Image Collection By Stefanie Waldek Published November 12, 2026 Look low in the northeastern sky on an autumn evening, and you might spot something unusual: a bright star flashing red, green, and blue. That’s Capella, one of the brightest stars in the night sky. But despite appearances, the star isn’t actually changing colors. The dazzling display is an optical effect caused by starlight passing through Earth’s atmosphere. And Capella isn’t the only star that puts on this kind of show. “Stars appear to twinkle or shimmer in the night sky, but this is not an inherent trait of stars,” says Emily Watson, astrophysicist and planetarium supervisor at the U.S. Space & Rocket Center. “As the light from a star passes through different densities and temperatures within our atmosphere, the light bends in a process called refraction.” The color flashes happen because Earth’s atmosphere bends different wavelengths of light by different degrees. pages.text: Los Mirlos: Tiny Desk Concert : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Los Mirlos: Tiny Desk Concert For more than 50 years, Los Mirlos has cultivated its own Peruvian twist on cumbia, featuring reverb-heavy, surf-rock guitar. Los Mirlos: Tiny Desk Concert September 17, 2026 10:00 AM ET Felix Contreras Credit: Photo: Vanessa Castillo/NPR From jazz and Tejano to norteño and ska, 'El Tiny' returns with a takeover from Sept. 15 to Oct. 15 for Latin Music Month . Originally born from Afro-Colombian communities, cumbia spread across the Spanish-speaking world , acquiring distinct musical accents along the way. In Peru, cumbia became particularly popular among oil workers deep in the Amazon. And when Jorge Rodriguez Grández started Los Mirlos in his small hometown of Moyobamba, his band played a regional style called cumbia amazónica, easily identifiable by its electric, reverb-heavy, surf-rock guitar. Throughout their performance, these cultural ambassadors share stories and declare their love for cumbia and their tropical homeland. We are so fortunate to host and share with you a group of true pioneers and innovators who, over 50 years later, still effortlessly pump out cumbia grooves. First of all, it was the final production of our sixth annual El Tiny series. This was a very emotional moment for a lot of reasons. People really love Los Tigres del Norte, to the point that playing their albums feels like sitting with family. And if you’ve seen the introduction I gave the band just before they played at the desk you can see that I wasn’t embarrassed to get emotional when I talked about what the band means to me. That emotional intro led to some changes in our process and format that resulted in a huge response from the audience that went viral. The result was a messy moment behind the scenes here at NPR and more than a little confusion for a lot of you. This week’s episode looks back at last week. First we want to share with you, directly from us, an explanation of what happened. But mostly we want to put the spotlight back on the band and their music because for decades they have been bringing out the kind emotions that got this whole thing started. Making a Better Battery Credit: Raw Pixel/Pixabay Helping smartphones hold their charge longer. Light-weight and energy-efficient, lithium-ion batteries have long been the battery of choice for powering smartphones, laptops, hoverboards, drones and other portable electronic devices. But even these low-maintenance batteries have their drawbacks—they lose their ability to hold charge after about 3 years, can catch on fire and often have to be recharged daily. To make a better lithium-ion battery or find innovative alternatives, PML researchers in collaboration with scientists from the Material Measurement Laboratory (MML) are studying how lithium batteries behave on some of the tiniest of scales, a few tens of atoms across. The scientists use an instrument that injects with exquisite precision an ultranarrow beam of lithium ions (charged atoms of lithium) into the negative terminal of a laboratory battery. pages.text: Man with venomous snakes and lizards stopped at German airport Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Man with suitcase full of snakes stopped at German airport 15 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Paulin Kola German Customs Not all the the snakes and lizards were alive, officials said A man has been stopped at Cologne Bonn Airport in Germany after trying to smuggle in more than 90 lizards and venomous snakes. Customs officials said the 45-year-old Mexican firefighter had looked "conspicuously nervous" as he tried to go through the green - nothing to declare - exit at the airport. They conducted a drugs test on the man - which came back positive for cocaine - before proceeding to check his suitcase. They did not find any drugs, but vipers, rattlesnakes and other species of snakes and lizards, including iguanas, hidden in shampoo and cream bottles, plastic containers and balls of socks. "My colleagues at the airport are used to a lot when it comes to souvenirs in suitcases, but we've never had 37 live venomous snakes and 55 lizards from Mexico before," said Jens Ahland, spokesman for the Cologne Customs office. Some were being kept "in inhumane conditions", Ahland said. Others had died during the journey from Mexico City via Istanbul. The man, who has not been named, told officers that he had brought the animals back as a favour for a Brazilian acquaintance. He was denied entry to Germany and flown back to Istanbul. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Monument Management Upper Missouri River Breaks National Monument was established by presidential proclamation on January 17, 2001, to protect an array of historical, geological, and biological resources. From Fort Benton to the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge, the monument spans 149 miles of the Upper Missouri River and encompasses 377,000 acres of adjacent Breaks country, including portions of Arrow Creek, Antelope Creek, and the Judith River. The monument includes six wilderness study areas, the Cow Creek Area of Critical Environmental Concern, segments of the Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail and the Nez Perce National Historic Trail, the Fort Benton National Historic Landmark, a watchable wildlife area, and the Missouri Breaks Back Country Byway. In 1976, Congress designated the Missouri River segment and corridor in this area a National Wild and Scenic River. In some areas, the BLM lands are intermingled with State of Montana lands and private property. The monument designation applies only to the BLM-managed lands. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Manatee Awareness Month: Protecting Gentle Giants at the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse Outstanding Natural Area Nov 3, 2026 Every November, Manatee Awareness Month celebrates one of Florida’s most beloved residents: the West Indian manatee. Often called “sea cows” because of their grazing habits, these gentle giants can grow to more than 10 feet long and weigh over 1,000 pounds. Despite their impressive size, manatees are peaceful, slow-moving animals that spend much of their time feeding on aquatic vegetation, resting, and traveling through coastal waters, rivers, estuaries, and springs. West Indian manatees swim in the clear, shallow waters of the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse Outstanding Natural Area in Jupiter, Florida. The Bureau of Land Management site is the only BLM-managed area where manatees are regularly observed and provides important habitat for these gentle marine mammals. pages.text: Manga Are Black, White and Read All Over. Treasures of the Globally Popular Japanese Comic Book Medium Are on View in New York Skip to main content The first rooms of the "Art of Manga" exhibition introduce visitors to manga, which is read right-to-left and usually published in black and white. Paula Abreu Pita Manga are Japanese comic books and graphic novels. They are typically written and illustrated by a single person, known as mangaka . They are usually printed in black and white and read right-to-left. And they are incredibly popular, in Japan and beyond. When Frederik L. Schodt, author of Manga! Manga! The World of Japanese Comics , published his book in the 1980s, “almost no one in the United States knew what manga was,” he tells the New York Times ’ Shivani Vora. Things have changed. Manga’s popularity is booming in the United States. “Today, young Americans have no problem with manga at all,” he says. “They are happy to read them Japanese-style, turning pages and viewing panels right-to-left.” More than 40 percent of Gen Z watches anime shows, which are often adaptations of manga, compared to just 25 percent who follow professional football. Now, the illustrated medium and its most well-known mangaka are the centerpiece of a new exhibition at the Brooklyn Museum in New York. “ Art of Manga ” is the country’s first large-scale show to explore the art form’s evolution, individual voices and cross-cultural impact. “The show’s focus on artists is what makes it so special. pages.text: Mario Balotelli: Why always him? The rise and fall of the Italian striker - BBC Sport By Jess Anderson BBC Sport journalist Maverick. Loose cannon. Unmanageable. Mario Balotelli heard it all. Perhaps better known for off-field antics than his undeniable - yet arguably wasted - talent with the ball at his feet, the Italian has always attracted headlines. Fifteen years have passed since his famous 'Why always me?' Manchester derby T-shirt celebration, which came just days after a firework was set off in his own bathroom, causing a house fire. The 36-year-old is still playing, now in the United Arab Emirates first division with Al-Ittifaq alongside his biological brother, Enock Barwuah. Here, BBC Sport looks at a career that has included 13 clubs, six countries - and an assist for arguably the most famous goal in Premier League history. Mancini to Mourinho - cracks begin to show Typical of his unconventional footballing life, Balotelli's career did not begin in an elite club's academy. Instead, by his mid-teens he was turning out for Italian third-tier side Lumezzane, close to the family home in Concesio. A trial at Barcelona did not lead to a long-term stay, and instead he was picked up by Inter Milan in 2006. It was at Inter that Balotelli first came across his great mentor - Roberto Mancini. The relationship between the two has been likened to that of a father and son. Under the Italian coach's tutelage, Balotelli flourished. pages.text: Marriage/Domestic Partnership | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Marriage/Domestic Partnership When you get married, you can change your health coverage. You can add yourself, your new spouse and children to your employer’s plan, enroll in your spouse’s employer’s plan, or find coverage through the Health Insurance Marketplace (Marketplace). Get the details on all of your special enrollment options and be sure you understand how the different plans work. You'll want to know the benefits covered, the amounts of any deductibles or copays you will be required to pay, what you will pay for premiums, and whether you can continue with the same doctors. For your retirement plan, when there is a change in your personal information, such as marriage, contact your plan administrator or the human resources department to change your status under the plan and provide them with updated contact information for you. Getting married also creates new financial demands that compete for retirement dollars, such as changing life insurance needs and saving to buy a home. But it's usually less expensive for two people to live together, thus freeing up dollars. A spending plan is essential. By: Rich Press March 9, 2021 Facebook Linkedin X.com Email To understand how something works, it helps to see it up close. A team of researchers took this approach when studying the fabric masks that people wear to slow the spread of COVID-19. Those masks work by blocking some of the virus-filled droplets and smaller particles, called aerosols, that an infected person exhales, and they also offer some protection to the wearer by filtering incoming air. The researchers wanted to know how well different fabrics filter out those particles and what makes some fabrics better filters than others. Their research indicates that that cotton fabrics tend to perform better than synthetics , with cotton flannels being particularly effective. After being exposed to the moisture in a person’s breath, cotton fabrics perform better still .
